# Jest Gotchas

> Known Jest patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Use runTestsByPath for Next.js app-router test paths](run-tests-by-path-for-nextjs-app-router-test-paths.md): Positional paths containing route-group parentheses or dynamic-segment brackets are parsed as regex patterns and can report that an existing test file was not found. MEDIUM.

- [A hand-written DB fake that ignores a column makes a bug look like correct behaviour](db-fake-ignores-column-hides-bug.md): A fake models only the columns someone remembered, so a column it omits reads as null and the resulting test asserts the defect as expected behaviour -- the suite then stays green through both the bug and its fix. Mirror every column the real statement writes, throw on unmatched queries, and back enum/width/CHECK expectations with a migration integration test. HIGH.

- [A fake that routes queries by a loose substring answers the wrong statement](loose-fixture-routing-answers-wrong-statement.md): The obvious discriminator -- a table name, COUNT(*), a column -- is often a substring of a sibling statement, so the fake answers the wrong query and the assertions pass against a query that never ran. Route on the predicate, order narrower matches first, and throw on anything unrouted. HIGH.

- [A patch bump can swap a transitive to ESM-only, and only Jest notices](patch-bump-swaps-transitive-to-esm-only.md): A patch release of a direct dependency moved one of its own dependencies onto an ESM-only major (sanitize-html 2.17.7 took htmlparser2 from dual-format v10 to ESM-only v12). Node 24 absorbs it via require(ESM) so the app, the build and a hand-run require all succeed -- Jest is the only consumer that cannot load it, and the stack trace accuses a CommonJS line in the innocent caller rather than the ESM package two levels down. Diff the two versions' dependency lists, not the file the trace names. HIGH.
